title: Mario 64's backwards long jump, explained
description: The BLJ is Super Mario 64's most famous speedrun glitch. Here is how it works and why Nintendo patched it later.

scenes.say: Super Mario 64 has a glitch where jumping backwards makes you absurdly fast. Speedrunners call it the B L J.

steps: Find a steep slope or stairs
scenes.say: The trick is repeated backwards long jumps on a steep slope or stairs. Each jump builds more speed.
Mario reaches very high speed values, far beyond what the designers intended. Speedrunners use that speed to skip huge parts of the game.
It saves enormous time, and it turned a small physics quirk into a core part of Mario 64 speedrunning. Players practise it for hours, because one mistake costs the whole run.
It was patched in the 1997 Rumble Pak version and later re-releases, so speedrunners stick to the original. Follow for more speedrun secrets.
